images.title: Why the ground floor is 0
images.purpose: Show that the ground floor is the starting point, so it is numbered 0, with +1 above it and −1 below it.
images.composition: Three floor rows stacked in a short column at the centre, with a label to the right of each and plenty of white space.
images.exact_structure: One column of 3 equal floor rows, all the same width. The top row is filled teal #0072B2, the middle row is filled reddish purple #CC79A7 and sits on a thick grey #6B7280 line, the bottom row is filled amber #E69F00. Exactly 3 rows, 1 grey line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra floor, dot, arrow or row beyond the counts stated
unequal floor rows or unequal arrow lengths
images.takeaway: The ground floor is where we start, so its number is 0.
images.description: Three equal floor rows: teal +1 on top, a purple 0 on a thick grey line in the middle marked start here, and amber −1 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the floor where the lift starts and say its number.

image_decisions.why: The ground floor as the starting point is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
